newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO says lifted stake in Asian unit.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO says lifted stake in Asian unit.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO Holding NV bought 10 percent of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Asia in March, lifting its stake to 70 percent, a spokesman said on Wednesday.
But ABN AMRO spokesman Tanno Massar said the price would not be disclosed.
ABN AMRO bought the stake from Hong Kong's Guoco Group, which retains 30 percent.

Massar said the increased share of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Asia, formerly HG Asia, was not mentioned in the bank's recent annual report and the prospectus for its planned New York listing as these documents related to the 1996 year.
The prospectus shows that ABN AMRO paid 322 million guilders to buy 40.5 percent of HG Asia in April and July 1995.
It bought its initial stake of about 20 percent in 1994, two years after buying London securities house Hoare Govett.
Hoare Govett established a Hong Kong office in 1972 and, in 1992, the company was bought by its staff in partnership with the Guoco/Hong Leong group and renamed HG Asia.
